'''Pau Gasol Sáez''' {{post-nominals|OLY}}<ref>{{cite news |last1=Wiberg |first1=Pernilla |author1-link=Pernilla Wiberg |title=Olympians at the heart of the Olympic Games, a milestone decision was taken today |url=https://olympians.org/news/2037/olympians-at-the-heart-of-the-olympic-games-a-milestone-decision-was-taken-today/ |access-date=6 August 2026 |work=olympians.org |publisher=[[World Olympians Association]] |date=June 24, 2026 |language=en}}</ref> ({{IPA|ca|ˈpaw ɣəˈzɔl|lang}}, {{IPA|es|ˈpaw ɣaˈsol|lang}}; born July 6, 1980) is a Spanish former professional [[basketball]] player who played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for 18 seasons, primarily as a power forward. He was a six-time [[NBA All-Star Game|NBA All-Star]] and a four-time [[All-NBA team]] selection, twice on the second team and twice on the third team. Gasol won two [[NBA championship]]s with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in [[2009 NBA Finals|2009]] and [[2010 NBA Finals|2010]]. He was the [[NBA Rookie of the Year]] in 2002 with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], the first non-American to win that award. He is regarded as one of the greatest power forwards of all time and one of the greatest European players of all time.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/page/nbarankPFs/ranking-greatest-power-forwards-nba-history |title=All-Time #NBArank: Duncan tops list of best power forwards ever |date=January 15, 2016 |publisher=ESPN |access-date=January 15, 2016 |archive-date=June 11, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170611114137/http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/page/nbarankPFs/ranking-greatest-power-forwards-nba-history |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://hoopshype.com/lists/20-greatest-power-forwards-ever-the-hoopshype-list/ |title=20 greatest power forwards ever: The HoopsHype list |date=November 21, 2021 |publisher=hoopshype.com |access-date=November 21, 2021 |archive-date=December 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221205215644/https://hoopshype.com/lists/20-greatest-power-forwards-ever-the-hoopshype-list/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://hoopshype.com/lists/40-greatest-european-players-ever-the-hoopshype-list// |title=40 greatest European players ever: The HoopsHype list |work=HoopsHype |date=January 11, 2022 |publisher=hoopshype.com |access-date=January 11, 2022 |archive-date=January 11, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220111213130/https://hoopshype.com/lists/40-greatest-european-players-ever-the-hoopshype-list/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=January 17, 2022 |title=Top 25 European Basketball Players Of All-Time |url=https://homeofplaymakers.com/top-25-european-basketball-players-of-all-time/14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210526130041/https://homeofplaymakers.com/top-25-european-basketball-players-of-all-time/14/ |archive-date=May 26, 2021 |access-date=January 17, 2022 |publisher=homeofplaymakers.com}}</ref> He is the older brother of former NBA player [[Marc Gasol]].

Gasol was selected by the [[Atlanta Hawks]] with the third overall pick in the first round of the [[2001 NBA draft]], but his rights were traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies|Vancouver Grizzlies]]. He holds the Grizzlies' franchise record for free throws made and attempted.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Memphis Grizzlies Career Leaders |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/MEM/leaders_career.html |access-date=May 17, 2008 |publisher=Basketball-Reference.com |archive-date=August 22, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110822083735/http://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/MEM/leaders_career.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Following more than six seasons with Memphis, Gasol played for the Los Angeles Lakers (2008–2014), [[Chicago Bulls]] (2014–2016), [[San Antonio Spurs]] (2016–2019), and [[Milwaukee Bucks]] (2019).

Internationally, Gasol has won a [[FIBA World Cup]] title, three [[EuroBasket]] titles, two [[Basketball at the Summer Olympics|Olympic]] silver medals, and an [[Basketball at the 2016 Summer Olympics|Olympic]] bronze medal with the [[Spanish national basketball team]]. Gasol was named MVP of the [[FIBA Basketball World Cup Most Valuable Player|2006 FIBA World Cup]] and the 2009 and 2015 [[FIBA EuroBasket MVP|FIBA EuroBasket]]. Pau Gasol shares (with [[Krešimir Ćosić]]) the record for most EuroBasket MVP awards, with two each. Gasol is also the all-time leading scorer in the [[EuroBasket records#All-time leading scorers in total points scored|EuroBasket]].

In 2021, he became a member of the [[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://olympics.com/ioc/mr-pau-gasol |title=Mr Pau Gasol |last= |first= |website=The International Olympic Committee |date=August 8, 2021 |access-date=17 August 2021 |archive-date=August 17, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210817150310/https://olympics.com/ioc/mr-pau-gasol |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2023, it was announced that Gasol would be inducted into the [[Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/dirk-nowitzki-dwyane-wade-headline-naismith-hall-of-fame-class-of-2023|title=Dirk Nowitzki, Dwyane Wade headline Naismith Hall of Fame Class of 2023|website=NBA.com|agency=Associated Press|date=April 1, 2023|accessdate=April 1, 2023|archive-date=April 2, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230402235346/https://www.nba.com/news/dirk-nowitzki-dwyane-wade-headline-naismith-hall-of-fame-class-of-2023|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Early life==
Gasol was born in [[Barcelona]]. Both of his parents played basketball in organized leagues. His father Agustí, a nurse administrator, stood {{convert|6|ft|3|in}}, and his mother Marisa, a medical doctor, was {{convert|6|ft|1|in|m}}.<ref name="birth">{{Cite news |last=Chuck Culpepper |date=February 10, 2008 |title=The Tao of Pau |work=Los Angeles Times |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2008-feb-10-sp-gasol10-story.html |access-date=December 30, 2009 |archive-date=March 29, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100329092740/http://articles.latimes.com/2008/feb/10/sports/sp-gasol10 |url-status=live }} "One of my friends was working there" as an obstetrician, said Gasol's mother, Marisa, herself a doctor of internal medicine, "and I went to him to take my boy. It's such a beautiful hospital." (Marisa Sàez, Pau Gasol's mother, referring to the [[Hospital de Sant Pau]], Barcelona, Spain)</ref> When Gasol was born, his family was living in [[Cornellà de Llobregat|Cornellà]], although he was born in [[Barcelona]], at [[Hospital de Sant Pau|Sant Pau Hospital]],<ref name="birth" /> where both of his parents worked. When he was 6 years old, his family moved to a city close to Barcelona, [[Sant Boi de Llobregat]], where he spent the remainder of his childhood.<ref name="GasolHome">{{Cite web |title=Pau Gasol's Official Web Site |url=http://www.paugasol.com/ |access-date=May 17, 2008 |publisher=Nike |archive-date=November 11, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201111194818/http://www.paugasol.com/ |url-status=live }}</ref><!--One can find this on his bio at his official site. Unfortunately, since it's all Flash, it's impossible to link directly to it.--> Gasol was interested in football, but loved basketball. The first sport he played was actually [[Rugby union|rugby]], before switching to basketball.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pau Gasol Más perfiles |url=http://es.eurosport.yahoo.com/fot/ftxt/pau_gasol.html |access-date=July 6, 2005 |language=es |archive-date=June 17, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070617191745/http://es.eurosport.yahoo.com/fot/ftxt/pau_gasol.html |url-status=live }}</ref> He is described as "a family boy and the perfect student, a tad shy, and a bit of a joker."<ref name="GasolHome" />

He originally did not want to make sports his career. On the day that [[Magic Johnson]] announced his HIV-positive status in 1991, the 11-year-old Gasol, who had heard the news in school, decided that he wanted to be a doctor and find a cure for AIDS. He enrolled in medical school at the [[University of Barcelona]] in 1998, but left after one year as his basketball career at FC Barcelona advanced.<ref name="Jenkins Page 3">{{Cite magazine |last=Jenkins |first=Lee |date=March 29, 2010 |title=The power of Pau |page=3 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1167642/3/index.htm |access-date=March 26, 2010 |archive-date=March 28, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100328023153/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1167642/3/index.htm |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>[https://www.bbc.com/sport/olympics/17958490 Pau Gasol profile] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210924183026/https://www.bbc.com/sport/olympics/17958490 |date=September 24, 2021 }} - website of the national broadcaster [[BBC]]</ref><ref>[https://olympics.com/ioc/mr-pau-gasol-saez Mr Pau GASOL SÁEZ] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210926124730/https://olympics.com/ioc/mr-pau-gasol-saez |date=September 26, 2021 }} - website of the [[International Olympic Committee]]</ref>

==== 2005–2008: First All-Star appearance and franchise records ====
[[File:Pau gasol zz.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Gasol playing for the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]]]
In his fifth year with the Grizzlies, he became the franchise's all-time leading rebounder on March 24 against the [[2005–06 New York Knicks season|New York Knicks]] when he grabbed his 3,072nd rebound in a Grizzlies uniform.<ref name="nbabio" /> He made 29 consecutive free throw attempts from January 24 to 28, tying the second best mark in Grizzlies history, including two straight games going 12–12 from the line, tying the best single-game mark in franchise history.<ref name="nbabio" /> Gasol and the Grizzlies returned to the [[2006 NBA Playoffs|playoffs]] for the third time in his and his team's history. Once again, they were eliminated in the first round and did not win a single game against the [[2005–06 Dallas Mavericks season|Dallas Mavericks]].<ref name="NBA06">{{Cite web |title=NBA Playoffs 2006 |website=[[NBA.com]] |url=http://www.nba.com/playoffs2006/ |access-date=May 17, 2008 |archive-date=August 19, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100819112619/http://www.nba.com/playoffs2006/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

On February 9, 2006, making his first appearance, Gasol was selected to play in the [[2005–06 NBA season|2006]] [[NBA All-Star Game]] in [[Houston, Texas]] as a reserve center for the [[Western Conference (NBA)|Western Conference]]. ==Player profile==
[[File:Pau Gasol by Augustas Didzgalvis.jpg|left|thumb|200px|Gasol during [[EuroBasket 2011]]]]
Listed at {{convert|7|ft|0|in}},{{efn|Gasol was listed at {{convert|7|ft|0|in}} until 2019–20, when it increased by {{convert|1|in|spell=in}} after the NBA standardized measurements across the league.<ref name="case_11012019"/><ref name="Hudon">{{Cite news |last=Hudon |first=Jamie |date=September 26, 2019 |title=NBA cracking down on lying about players' height |work=NBCSports.com |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/northwest/portland-trail-blazers/nba-cracking-down-lying-about-players-height |access-date=September 14, 2020 |archive-date=October 26, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211026233753/https://www.nbcsports.com/northwest/portland-trail-blazers/nba-cracking-down-lying-about-players-height |url-status=live }}</ref>}} Gasol was athletic for his size, allowing him to play both the power forward and center positions, much like fellow European players [[Toni Kukoč]] and [[Dirk Nowitzki]]. He was a refined scorer in the post and midrange; his overall game was near-[[ambidextrous]], making it difficult for opposing teams to defend. Gasol used a variety of midrange jumpers, hook shots, up-and-under moves, and shot fakes to score very efficiently. In addition, his foot speed relative to his size allowed him to run the fast break and finish effectively. He was also a skilled passer for a big man,<ref name=trudell_04102013/> earning 3.2 assists per game over his career. Defensively, he is an above-average shot blocker with a career average of 1.7 blocks per game. Kobe Bryant said of Gasol, "You'd be hard-pressed to find a big [man] with his skill set in the history of the game."<ref name=trudell_04102013/>

Gasol recorded over 550 double-doubles in his NBA career.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pau Gasol Game Finder |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/play-index/pgl_finder.cgi |website=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=December 29, 2019 |archive-date=November 1, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091101130223/https://www.basketball-reference.com/play-index/pgl_finder.cgi |url-status=live }}</ref> On April 2, 2016, he became the 36th player in NBA history to reach the 10,000-point/10,000-rebound mark.<ref name="pistons-loss" /> While Gasol became the 43rd player in NBA history to reach to the 20,000-point milestone, he is just the fourth with that many points, 10,000 rebounds, 3,500 assists and 1,500 blocks.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 12, 2017 |title=Pau Gasol joins rare NBA company with 20,000th career point |url=http://www.sportingnews.com/nba/news/pau-gasol-20000-points-spurs-nba-history/nls5xr8kbb1t1xtkbb0z4wfos |access-date=April 14, 2017 |website=sportingnews.com |archive-date=April 14, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170414081358/http://www.sportingnews.com/nba/news/pau-gasol-20000-points-spurs-nba-history/nls5xr8kbb1t1xtkbb0z4wfos |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Personal life==
[[File:Pau Gasol Santa Maria.jpg|right|thumb|150px|Gasol in 2008]]
Gasol remains strongly interested in medicine. He regularly visits [[Children's Hospital of Los Angeles]], a standard stop for athletes making charitable visits in the L.A. area, but does not limit his business to visiting young patients. On one visit, he asked a group of doctors well-informed questions about their treatment of children with [[scoliosis]]. In April 2010, Gasol was scheduled to sit in on a spinal surgery, wearing surgical scrubs, with Dr. David Skaggs, the hospital's chief of orthopedic surgery. Skaggs has said, "We talk to him now almost like he is a surgical colleague."<ref name="Jenkins Page 1">{{Cite magazine |last=Jenkins |first=Lee |date=March 29, 2010 |title=The power of Pau |page=1 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1167642/index.htm |access-date=March 26, 2010 |archive-date=March 28, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100328042948/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1167642/index.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref> Gasol canceled his original plans to observe a surgery when he came down with a low-grade fever the day before the operation, not wishing to risk infecting anyone at the hospital. He was able to reschedule his observation for June 2010, witnessing Skaggs lead a team operating on a 13-year-old girl from Colorado with scoliosis.<ref name="Dr. Gasol">{{Cite web |last=Friend |first=Tom |date=August 6, 2010 |title=Dr. Gasol? Pau's love outside basketball |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/columns/story?columnist=friend_tom&page=drgasol-100806 |access-date=August 7, 2010 |publisher=ESPN |archive-date=August 18, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100818015558/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/columns/story?columnist=friend_tom&page=drgasol-100806 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Gasol has a broad range of intellectual and cultural interests. He has taught himself Italian and French<ref name="Jenkins Page 1" /> to go along with his childhood languages of [[Catalan language|Catalan]] and Spanish plus English. While with the Lakers, he and [[Kobe Bryant]] spoke to one another during games in Spanish to keep opponents from knowing their plans.<ref name="Jenkins Page 3" /> Gasol also regularly reads historical novels, plays French classical music on his keyboard, and attends concerts and operas; he is a friend of Spanish tenor [[Plácido Domingo]], and often visits him backstage after performances.<ref name="Jenkins Page 1" />

Gasol married Catherine McDonnell in July 2019. He posted a photo of his wedding on his Instagram account.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pau on Instagram: "The most magical moment I've experienced in my entire life. ==Work and social commitment==
In 2003, he was named a [[UNICEF]] ambassador,<ref>{{Cite web |last1=May 21 |last2=valores |first2=2012 {{!}} Educación |last3=NBA |last4=basket |first4=Protagonistas |last5=Esc |first5=Victor |last6=Ón {{!}} 0 {{!}} |date=May 21, 2012 |title=Pau Gasol, un jugador comprometido socialmente {{!}} {{!}} JGBasket |url=https://jgbasket.net/pau-gasol-un-jugador-comprometido-socialmente/ |access-date=October 21, 2019 |website=jgbasket.net |language=es |archive-date=April 6, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190406132204/https://jgbasket.net/pau-gasol-un-jugador-comprometido-socialmente/ |url-status=live }}</ref> and since then has repeatedly taken part in different campaigns, traveling on several occasions África to participate in its projects there. In recognition of his commitment to solidarity endeavors, he received the ''Corazón de Oro'' (Gold Heart) in 2004, awarded by the Spanish Heart Foundation,<ref>{{Cite web |last=FEC |title=Pau Gasol |url=https://fundaciondelcorazon.com/prevencion/88-testimonios-famosos/1006-pau-gasol.html |access-date=October 21, 2019 |website=Fundación Española del Corazón |language=es-es |archive-date=October 21, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191021202543/https://fundaciondelcorazon.com/prevencion/88-testimonios-famosos/1006-pau-gasol.html |url-status=live }}</ref> and the 2010 Charitable Athlete Prize, given by the Fundación SOS. Gasol has worked in support of infant survival and for the rights of children in other African countries as well as in campaigns against malnutrition in the Horn of Africa. In addition, since his arrival in Memphis, he has worked with the Saint Jude Children's Research Hospital, which he visits every time he in the city where he lived at the start of his career.

In 2009, Gasol, along with several other NBA players, joined the "Hoops for St. Jude" charity program benefitting the [[St. Jude Children's Research Hospital]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Berger |first=Ken |date=March 4, 2010 |title=St. Jude utilizes power of Love, NBA in fight against cancer |publisher=CBSsports.com |url=http://www.cbssports.com/nba/story/13009170/st-jude-utilizes-power-of-love-nba-in-fight-against-cancer |url-status=dead |access-date=March 20, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130902120224/http://www.cbssports.com/nba/story/13009170/st-jude-utilizes-power-of-love-nba-in-fight-against-cancer |archive-date=September 2, 2013}}</ref>

In 2010, UNICEF's Pau Project commenced in Ethiopia, to aid in the fight against infant malnutrition, which each year claims the lives of more than 2 million children, and for the right to an education. In December 2010 he took part, along with other NBA stars, in We Are Bigger Than Aids, a campaign against the HIV virus.<ref>{{Cite web |last=AS |first=Diario |date=December 1, 2010 |title=Pau Gasol, comprometido en la lucha contra el Sida |url=https://as.com/baloncesto/2010/12/01/mas_baloncesto/1291158011_850215.html |access-date=October 21, 2019 |website=AS.com |language=es |archive-date=October 21, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191021202541/https://as.com/baloncesto/2010/12/01/mas_baloncesto/1291158011_850215.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2012, the Professional Basketball Writers Association (PBWA) stated that Pau "personifies everything that is good about NBA players and their charity projects, not only in their own communities but all over the world, working to help children achieve their goals and have the opportunities that they wouldn't be able to get otherwise." Thus, in April 2015, they gave him their [[Magic Johnson Award]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 22, 2015 |title=Pau Gasol wins the 2014-15 Magic Johnson Award Professional Basketball Writers Association |url=http://probasketballwriters.org/pau-gasol-wins-magic-johnson-award/ |access-date=October 21, 2019 |website=Professional Basketball Writers Association |language=en-US |archive-date=October 21, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191021202543/http://probasketballwriters.org/pau-gasol-wins-magic-johnson-award/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In September 2018, after the publication of his book ''Bajo el aro'' (Under the Hoop) Gasol said that in spite of not being a doctor, he tries to use his public profile to help others.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 5, 2018 |title=Pau Gasol: "No pude ser médico, así que utilizo mi perfil público para ayudar" |url=https://www.abc.es/deportes/baloncesto/abci-baloncesto-gasol-no-pude-medico-utilizo-perfil-publico-para-ayudar-201809051858_noticia.html |access-date=October 21, 2019 |website=abc |language=es |archive-date=October 21, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191021202542/https://www.abc.es/deportes/baloncesto/abci-baloncesto-gasol-no-pude-medico-utilizo-perfil-publico-para-ayudar-201809051858_noticia.html |url-status=live }}</ref> That same month, he joined the campaign of Spain's Fundación Atresmedia to bring families into schools.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 13, 2018 |title=Pau Gasol, protagonista de la campaña de la Fundación Atresmedia y Gasol Foundation para acercar la familia a la escuela |url=https://www.europapress.es/epsocial/responsables/noticia-pau-gasol-protagonista-campana-fundacion-atresmedia-gasol-foundation-acercar-familia-escuela-20180913140755.html |access-date=October 21, 2019 |publisher=Europa Press |archive-date=October 21, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191021202542/https://www.europapress.es/epsocial/responsables/noticia-pau-gasol-protagonista-campana-fundacion-atresmedia-gasol-foundation-acercar-familia-escuela-20180913140755.html |url-status=live }}</ref>
